newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Technocrat beats Communist in Siberian election.
newsitem.headline: Technocrat beats Communist in Siberian election.

text.p: The mayor of Russia's Siberian city of Irkutsk has won a local election to become governor of the vast industrial region, beating a Communist rival, Interfax news agency said on Monday.

It said according to unofficial final results from Sunday's polls, Boris Govorin won just over 50 percent of the vote. Local Communist Party chief Sergei Levchenko trailed way behind on 19 percent, while six other candidates scored modestly.
Govorin stood as an independent candidate but was supported by the regional branch of the pro-government Our Home is Russia party and by the incumbent governor Yuri Nozhikov.
The campaign in the eastern Siberian region was overshadowed by mud-slinging but there was no indication of serious violations on polling day.

It was the second upset for the Communists this month. Pro-government reformist Ivan Sklyarov beat a Communist rival to win the governorship of Nizhny Novgorod on July 13 in a contest seen as a litmus test for Russia's liberal reforms.

The outcome in Irkutsk, one of the few Russian regions which contribute to the federal budget rather than living on government subsidies, has also been seen as indicative of the general political situation in the country.
As governor, Govorin will also sit in the Federation Council, the upper chamber of parliament which is made up of influential regional bosses.

The Irkutsk and Nizhny Novgorod results, which both promoted mayors to top political posts, also showed that top local bureaucrats who demonstrate no definite political affiliation but have a "get-things-done" image are increasingly gaining influence in Russia.
Moscow mayor Yuri Luzhkov, widely seen as a strong potential candidate at the next presidential election, is another example of such a trend.
Three months ago Nozhikov, elected governor in 1994, said he was resigning from the post, citing the worsening social and economic situation in the region.
